rationale: See hive/EMPEROR.md tick 0. Two kings split the problem at its natural seam: WORLD (what HER2, VHHs and the phage-NGS-cryoEM assay physically are, and what the organisers actually measure) vs INFER (how to turn sequence + public structure + NGS into per-residue probabilities, how to validate with only 3 test complexes, and what other fields know). Nine queens x five workers keeps every king under ~5 queen digests. Deadline is 2026-10-31 so rounds are short and modeling runs in parallel with research.

kings.name: King WORLD - the biology, the molecules and the measurement
kings.mandate: Everything about HER2, ERBB family biology, VHH/nanobody immunology and structure, the phage-display + NGS + cryo-EM ground-truth chain, and the challenge as an institution. Owns the question 'what exactly is the label, and what is it confounded with?'
cross_domain_lenses: forensic science and chain of custody (how trustworthy is an enrichment label?)
law of evidence and burden of proof (what counts as an epitope?)
ecology and niche modelling (binding as occupancy of a surface niche)
art conservation and restoration (inferring the original from degraded traces)
healthcare screening statistics (base rates, PR vs ROC, prevalence ~0.1)

queens.subdomain: HER2/ERBB2 and the ERBB family: ectodomain domains I-IV, dimerisation, signalling, cancer, antibody drugs, glycosylation and PTMs, isoforms, transcripts, epigenetics, adjacent proteins, and every known HER2 epitope and structure

Camelid heavy-chain antibodies and VHH: germline genes, CDR1-3 geometry, convex vs concave paratopes, somatic hypermutation, immunisation, known paratope rules, therapeutic nanobodies, and every known HER2 nanobody

The measurement chain: alpaca immunisation, phage display biopanning (one round), NGS read counts, chi-squared enrichment labels, AVIDa-hHER2 anatomy, and the cryo-EM + Voronota-LT ground truth. Noise, bias, controls, gotchas
SEPIQ 2026 as an institution: guidelines, organisers, Hugging Face space and dataset, baseline, ambiguities and contradictions, CAPRI track, precedents, leaderboard and community

kings.name: King INFER - from sequence to interface
kings.mandate: Everything about turning sequence, public structures and NGS enrichment into per-residue epitope and paratope probabilities and winning Track A: methods, data representation and integration (the user's breakthrough hypothesis), validation with only three test complexes, compute, and cross-domain ideas.
cross_domain_lenses: the CASP history of protein folding (what changed it: data representation, MSAs, end-to-end training)
music information retrieval (alignment of two sequences with local correspondence)
sports analytics (small-n evaluation, ranking with huge noise)
philosophy of science (what a held-out set of three can and cannot tell you)

queens.subdomain: Co-folding and docking for VHH-antigen: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, OpenFold3, Protenix, HADDOCK, ClusPro, ZDOCK; nanobody-specific benchmarks and failure modes; confidence metrics and seed sampling; turning a predicted complex into per-residue probabilities

Sequence-based and structure-based epitope/paratope predictors and protein language models: BepiPred-3, DiscoTope-3, SEMA, EpiPred, AbEpiTope, ESM-2/3, AbLang, nanoBERT, IgLM, AntiBinder, transfer learning and leakage in antibody datasets

The breakthrough hypothesis: how to represent and integrate the 1.8M-read NGS enrichment data and other public data (clonotype families, convergent CDR3, co-enrichment, coevolution between paratope and epitope, DMS, mimotopes, structure ensembles) so weak binding signal becomes interface signal

How to actually compete in 14 days: validation design with only three held-out complexes, public HER2 complexes as proxies, leakage control, compute plan across Explorer/Modal/Kaggle/Colab/OpenProtein/Boltz, the five-submission ladder, uncertainty and ensembling, day-by-day runbook

What other fields know about inferring an interface from weak, noisy, enrichment-like signals, and about winning small-n blind challenges. Analogies from folding history, cryptanalysis, ecology, law, art, music, sports, healthcare, linguistics
